descriptionChirho: Qal stative sense: to be holy, become holy, or attain a state of holiness — the inherent condition of sacredness (Arabic قَدُسَ qadusa; Swahili -takatifu stative; Korean 거룩해지다).

Niphal passive-reflexive sense: to be sanctified, shown holy, or vindicated as holy — typically of God manifesting His holiness among the nations (Arabic أَتَقَدَّسُ / يَتَقَدَّسُ reflexive form V; Korean 거룩하게 되다; Swahili -takaswa passive).

Piel factitive/declarative sense: to make holy, sanctify, consecrate, or declare sacred — an agent actively imparts holiness to a person, object, or time (Arabic قَدَّسَ qaddasa intensive form II; Korean 거룩하게 하다; Swahili -takasa transitive).

Pual passive sense: to have been consecrated, sanctified, or set apart — the resultant state of having been made holy by another agent (Arabic مُقَدَّس muqaddas passive participle; Korean 거룩하게 된; Swahili -takaswa/-wekwa wakfu passive).

Hifil causative sense: to dedicate, devote, set apart for sacred use, or consecrate to God — emphasizing the act of devoting persons, spoils, or objects to divine service (Arabic قَدَّسَ / أَقْدَسَ causative; Korean 구별하다/드리다 set apart/offer; Swahili -weka wakfu dedicate).

Hitpael reflexive sense: to sanctify oneself, consecrate oneself, undergo ritual purification — the subject performs the act of consecration upon themselves in preparation for divine encounter or sacred service (Arabic تَقَدَّسَ taqaddasa reflexive form V; Korean 거룩하게 하다 자신을; Swahili -jitakasa reflexive).

Nominal sense: holy things, consecrated objects, or sanctuaries — used as a noun referring to sacred items or sacred places belonging to someone (Arabic أَقْدَاس / مَقَادِس holy things/sanctuaries; Korean 거룩한 것들/곳들; Swahili vitu vitakatifu / mahali patakatifu).
